executive_summary: Canada is experiencing an unprecedented ransomware crisis with over 100 Canadian organizations compromised in a single 48-hour period. High-profile victims include Canada Goose (consumer goods), National Money Mart (financial services with database leaked), Peterborough Public Health, Eastern Townships School Board, Municipality of North Perth, and MRC de Maskinongé district government. The Qilin ransomware group leads the attack wave with 19 victims, followed by Play (11 victims), Clop (13 victims), and SafePay (11 victims). This coordinated surge across critical sectors—including healthcare, education, public sector, and financial services—represents a national-scale cyber emergency requiring immediate incident response and federal coordination.

canada_landscape.summary: Canada is under massive ransomware siege with 100+ organizations compromised across all critical sectors in 48 hours. High-impact victims include Canada Goose, National Money Mart (database leaked), three public health/municipal entities (Peterborough Public Health, Municipality of North Perth, MRC de Maskinongé), Eastern Townships School Board, and multiple financial services firms. No CCCS advisories were issued in this reporting period despite the national emergency.
canada_landscape.retailers: Canada Goose (consumer goods/retail) compromised by CoinbaseCartel ransomware; Active Green + Ross (automotive retail) compromised by Sinobi ransomware
canada_landscape.financial: National Money Mart Company compromised by Everest ransomware with database leaked; Morison Insurance Brokers compromised by Sinobi ransomware; Trucash (financial services) compromised by Lynx ransomware; Axion50plus (financial services) compromised by Devman ransomware; multiple accounting/CPA firms including Pewarchuk CPA (Play) and MG Chartered Professional Accountant (Qilin)

report_2w.executive_summary: Canadian government (CCCS) issued two critical alerts this week: CVE-2026-45659 affecting Microsoft SharePoint Server and CVE-2026-8451 impacting Citrix NetScaler, both requiring immediate patching. The Canadian spy agency disclosed it successfully hacked a ransomware gang, drug traffickers, and extremists last year. A major Canadian data breach lawsuit was filed against Alberta and Centurion Project affecting millions of voters. Three new ransomware groups—Genesis, Avalon (deploying CrownX), and continued activity from Qilin and Akira—are actively targeting healthcare, real estate, and tech sectors. ShinyHunters breached Medtronic exposing 3.8 million patient records and Moody Bible Institute affecting 2.3 million accounts.
